## Survey open-0: LIN-4451 @ c205190fd

Read in LinearViewer at `c205190fd`. Piece 1 (LIN-4450) is already merged here, and nothing else since `4b5001ddf` touches the plan's paths.

**Why this will be hard**

1. **`parentId` (note 5) is not a Jira problem.** `routes/proxy-writes.js:451–459` *skips* any non-UUID `parentId`/`assigneeId`/`cycleId`. It does not refuse them, and the `writable` gate never runs for them. Linear already loses `parentId: "LIN-123"` this way, and PATCH does the same (`:542–544`). Option (b) is the honest fix, but it changes Linear too. Option (a) alone leaves Linear's silent drop in place. I'd pick (b) and note the cross-provider effect on LIN-4445.

2. **Epic routing has no input to decide on.** "Use `parent` on team-managed, Epic Link on company-managed" needs a per-project style check, and nothing in `lib/providers/jira/` reads one (no `style`, `simplified` or `next-gen`). `_resolveEpicLinkFieldId` is tenant-wide, so the field existing doesn't mean this project's create screen has it. The read side tries `fields.parent` first and falls back to Epic Link. I'd write the same way: send `parent`, and use Epic Link only when the chosen type's createmeta lists it. No style lookup needed. Also, `updateIssue` refuses `projectId` (D4), so an epic set at create can't be changed later.

3. **The createmeta cache is the provider's first cross-request state.** Its current code says "per-call only, no cross-request cache." OAuth scopes may have no `site` (`_clientFor` ~415 requires only `cloudId`), so a site-only key can collide. Createmeta is filtered by the caller's permissions, so one cache per site can offer a type this user can't create. Key on `cloudId || site` plus project, with a short TTL.

4. **The Periodical gate (note 4) is wider than `issueWriteGuard`.** I checked: the gate marker survives `holdAsAsked` → `readDescription`, and `states()` returns `type: 'completed'`, so the gate can fire. But taking "the last 20 comments from the same `getIssue`" relies on Jira's embedded `fields.comment`, which is oldest-first and capped. On a busy ticket the evidence comments could be missing. Use `client.listComments` and take the tail. Bodies need `adfToMarkdown`.

5. **One retirement may be wrong.** `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s "where the provider cannot create tickets" branch is still true for `github-projects`, which has no `createIssue`. Retire it only if that provider can't be dispatched. Otherwise keep it and say why.

6. **Missed surfaces.** `lib/proxy-instructions.js:791` lists the create fields each provider refuses and needs a Jira line. The feedback lane sends `FEEDBACK_PROJECT_ID` (a Linear id) to any provider as `projectId`, with no `apiWriteFields()` check (`workspace-api-feedback.js` ~470). On Jira it refuses screenshots with 422 (no `uploadFile`).

**What I'd do first**

Before any code, post the `parentId` disposition and the epic-write rule as a comment on LIN-4445. Both change the plan: (b) reaches Linear, and the epic rule drops the style split. Then build the client and fake `createIssue`/`getCreateMeta`, testing the issue-type picker and the required-field 422 first as pure functions. Do the retirements and prompt re-measure last, since the `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` and `periodicals.js` wording edits move both the budget test and the Periodical hash.

## Survey global: LIN-4451 @ c205190fd

Read at `origin/main` c205190fd. Piece 1 (LIN-4450) has already landed there.

**Where it lands.** `lib/providers/jira/index.js` is improving. LIN-4450 gave the seal one owner (`as-asked-region.js`), and every read goes through it. But much of the file's comment describes limits the code no longer has. The three filing lanes are worse:
- `routes/proxy-writes.js` ~400–470 refuses a field the provider doesn't declare.
- `routes/workspace-api-issue-write.js` ~750–800 drops it silently.
- `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js` ~440–515 passes a raw `teamId`, resolved by nothing.

Each re-implements team, seal and field forwarding with its own resolver, and they have taken 33 commits since October. Jira lands in three places, not one.

**What the obvious way does.**
- **Stale plan steps.** There is no `inlineCreate: false` to retire: it already derives from `supports('createIssue')` (`interface.js:229`). `docs/proxy-integration.md:2075` already says Jira holds the block.
- **A wrong retirement.** `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s "where the provider cannot create tickets" stays true. GitHub Projects is live and read-only, with no `createIssue`. Keep it and cite it.
- **Missed second copies.** `docs/architecture/source-map.md:83` repeats "createIssue deferred behind LIN-1557". The NOTE at `interface.js:214–218` says `supports('createIssue')` "is intentionally false this phase", which is already wrong for Linear, Local and GitHub.
- **A noisy check.** The plan's grep matches about 40 lines in `docs/papers` JSON. Scope it to `lib routes README.md docs/proxy-integration.md docs/architecture`.
- **Feedback lane.** It forwards the deployment env `FEEDBACK_TEAM_ID` and `FEEDBACK_PROJECT_ID` (Linear UUIDs) to any provider. Once Jira can create, a server with those set hands Jira a UUID as project key and as epic. With them unset, feedback goes to whichever project `fetchTeams()` returns first. Screenshots 422, because Jira has no `uploadFile`. A fake e2e test that doesn't set the env won't show this.
- **New state.** The issue-type cache would be the provider's first cross-request state. The provider is per-call by design (`_resolveEpicLinkFieldId`: "no cross-request cache"). `lib/` already holds about ten hand-rolled `*-cache.js` files and no shared TTL helper, so an inline `Map` would be one more copy.

**Symptom vs. cause.**
- **Note 5 is one case of a pattern.** `present: isUuid` silently skips any non-UUID `assigneeId`, `parentId` or `cycleId`. Disposition (b), a 400 for a present-but-malformed value, fixes all three in one line.
- **Note 4 is the same shape.** `issueWriteGuard` has no declared shape. The gate reads Linear's GraphQL `comments.nodes`, and GitHub and Local return no `description`, so the Periodical gate works only on Linear. Fixing Jira alone copies that Linear-shaped object into a second provider.

**Better, within reach.**
- Take (b) for all UUID-gated fields.
- Apply the feedback env team and project only on Linear, or resolve them through `resolveTeamInput`.
- Cut the Jira header down to what is true.
- Fix the `interface.js` NOTE and `source-map.md`. Keep the `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` branch.
- If the gate is in scope, declare `description` and `comments` on the guard in `interface.js`.

**Better still, not this task's.** One create pipeline shared by the three lanes, with one resolver and one refuse-or-drop policy. Also one shared TTL cache.

## LIN-4451: done. PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2429

Head `78fd12cad`, branch `feat/lin-4451-jira-create-lanes`, based on main `5dcf5bcda`. CI green on the head: Unit tests, Unit tests (proxy, clock +400d), E2E shards 1-4/4, Secret scan, and the aggregate `CI success`.

**Built.** Jira `createIssue` (project = team, epic = `projectId`) opens three lanes: proxy create (also the Periodical mint), session create (in-app form), and feedback intake. Details and decisions are in the PR body and the commit message.

**Decisions taken, and where the plan changed** (also on LIN-4445):
- `parentId`, review note 5: disposition (b) on the create lanes. A present non-UUID `assigneeId`, `parentId` or `cycleId` is a 400, not a silent drop. This changes Linear: an issue key in `parentId` on create is now refused. PATCH still drops it silently; follow-up.
- Epic write: `parent` when the create screen offers it, else Epic Link. Read from this project's screen.
- No create-metadata cache (departs from the plan's "cache briefly"; reason in the PR).
- Feedback env defaults are not applied on Jira.

**Retired:** the Jira external deep-link create path (the override stays as the `ui.write` gate only), the LIN-1557 deferral comments and the stale `interface.js` NOTE, README's "creating new issues isn't supported yet", `source-map.md`'s deferral, and the "Linear task" wording in the Periodical prompts (16 hashes re-pinned, reason in the test). `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s "cannot create tickets" branch is kept: GitHub Projects is still read-only.

**Open, not decided:** a Jira screenshot is still refused 422 (no `uploadFile`; an attachment needs an issue first). Jira feedback with no env default files to the first Jira project. Both are recorded in `docs/areas/providers.md` and `web-routes.md` Waiting.

**Evidence:** 1644 targeted unit tests passed locally on the first commit; three mutations each failed their witness; the CI-only failures (lin-4119 header case, Jira F4 E2E) were fixed and reproduced locally before pushing. Live Jira acceptance of a create with `properties` or a `parent` is still unverified and is LIN-4452's check.

### Leftovers
- `lib/providers/jira/index.js`, constructor comment on `site`: still called `getCreateTaskUrl` the "+ Add task" link, and missed the `_resolveSite` fallback. Tidied.
- `tests/unit/render.test.js`, the "Jira external deep-link branch" pin: no in-tree provider takes that branch now. Heading and describe name tidied.
- `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, the `getCreateTaskUrl` sentence: still described it as the "+ Add task" link. Tidied.
- `lib/render.js`, the external deep-link "+ Add task" branch now has no in-tree provider, and the four `getCreateTaskUrl` overrides only gate `ui.write`. Larger than a fix: noted in `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md`.
- `routes/workspace-api-issue-write.js`, "an undeclared create field is a 400" is spelled three ways across the lanes, and feedback picks env defaults by provider name. Noted in `docs/areas/web-routes.md`.
- `lib/task-share-store.js`, the share-token store still has its own sha256 helper, the same digest as the new `hashHarbourToken`. Noted in `docs/areas/auth-accounts-and-workspaces.md`.
- Lesson added to `docs/areas/agent-api.md`: a format check on an optional create field refuses with 400, never as the field's `present` gate.
Retires: `routes/proxy.js`: `hashCredential` (proxyLimiter's key) is a second sha256-of-a-token helper. The three token stores and the proxy limiter now share `hashHarbourToken` from `lib/harbour-token-format.js`. Tests pin the digest and that no copy remains; the pin was seen to fail with a copy reintroduced.

## Review — LIN-4451

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2429 at head `466e8a462d7dc0fdd2867f2b13c4696c1e8a7671` (OPEN, MERGEABLE).

CI: green on head `466e8a462`: Unit tests, Unit tests (proxy, clock +400d), E2E shards 1–4/4, Secret scan (source), CI success. Locally I also ran 11 targeted suites (lin-4451, proxy-create-write-contract, jira-provider, providers, render, render-task-create, task-create-route, periodicals, lin-4313 Periodical bytes, prompt-size-budget, harbour-token-format): 868/868 pass.

**Staleness:** no commits on the plan's paths since the ticket was created other than LIN-4450 (#2421), which this work builds on. **Regression check:** `git log` on the touched routes, provider and periodicals files shows no reverts, and nothing earlier is re-applied. The LIN-4390 hand-off bullet is intact; only "in Linear" was removed from it.

### Open question from the brief: the Periodical gate (review note 4) is **fixed in this PR, not filed**
`issueWriteGuard` (`lib/providers/jira/index.js` ~1031) now returns `description` (through `readDescription`) and `comments.nodes`: the last 20 from `listAllComments`, as Markdown via `adfToMarkdown`, fetched only when the gate marker is present. That shape matches what `refusedByPeriodicalGate` reads (`routes/proxy-writes.js:488–503`) and Linear's `comments(last: 20) { nodes { id body } }`. The unit witness only checks the guard's shape, so I also ran a temporary **route-level** repro on the Jira fake. I PATCHed `stateId: 'done'` on a gate-marked issue that had no report comment: **409 `PERIODICAL_REPORT_NOT_PERSISTED`** on head, and **200** with the guard's `description` mutated away. The gate fires end to end on Jira.

### Against what was asked (each sentence of `## As asked`)
- *Piece 2 of 3 … adds Jira issue creation, which opens all three filing lanes (proxy, session and feedback; Periodical mints and last-step filings use proxy create)*: met. `createIssue` is in client, fake and provider. Lane tests go through the real routes: proxy create, including a Periodical-mint shape with `teamId: 'ENG'`; session create `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/issues`; and feedback intake.
- *…and retires what creation makes obsolete*: met (see Retires below).
- *Blocked by piece 1*: LIN-4450 is Done and merged (`2bf788b6d`).
- *Read the parent's plan + Plan Review Verdict notes 4 and 5*: both dispositioned. Note 5 took **(b)** (non-UUID `assigneeId`/`parentId`/`cycleId` is a 400 on create; `parentId` is not declared on Jira, so subtasks are not advertised). Note 4 is **fixed** (above).
- *Starting point … where the code shows it wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4445*: done. The departures were posted on LIN-4445 per the 16:23 comment: (b) reaches Linear, epic routing is read from the create screen rather than project style, no createmeta cache, and feedback env defaults are skipped on Jira.
- *Approach 1 (client + fake)*: met. Instead of a single `getCreateMeta`, the client has `listCreateIssueTypes` and `listCreateIssueTypeFields`, both paged.
- *Approach 2 (provider create, re-read with `properties=harbour.asAsked`, `createFields` = title/description/teamId, `apiWriteFields` + `projectId`, no `stateId`)*: met. A failed re-read is a `PartialWriteError` ("do not retry"), which is good.
- *Approach 3 (issue type; 422 naming required fields; "cache briefly per site and project")*: type choice and the 422 are met. **The cache is not built, and that is a deliberate departure.** createmeta is permission-filtered, so a site-keyed cache can serve one caller's types to another (Survey open-0 point 3). The reason is recorded in the `createIssue` docblock, in `docs/areas/providers.md` and on LIN-4445. It changes cost, not behaviour, and the plan's own "Change course and say so" clause covers it. I accept it.
- *Approach 4 (Periodical gate)*: met (above).
- *Approach 5 (UI; keep `getCreateTaskUrl`)*: met. The override is kept as the `ui.write` gate. The E2E F4 test now pins the in-app `/task/new?projectId=` href, with no `CreateIssue` or `pid=`.
- *Approach 6 (Retires)*: met, with one justified exception. The plan's grep, scoped as the Survey advised (`lib routes README.md docs/proxy-integration.md docs/architecture`), leaves only LIN-1557 hits about the headless write contract, all still true, plus `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. That branch is kept because GitHub Projects is live and read-only, as both Surveys found. README (both lines), `source-map.md`, the `interface.js` NOTE, the Jira header, profile and `getCreateTaskUrl` docblocks, and the "Linear task" Periodical wording are all retired. `inlineCreate: false` never existed as a literal, so there was nothing to retire there (Survey global).
- *Approach 7 (prompt re-measure)*: met. prompt-size-budget and lin-4313 pass, with 16 hashes re-pinned and the reason recorded in the test.
- *Testing strategy*: met. The parent-path test is correctly omitted, since (a) was not taken. One witness is weak; see Fixes.
- *Done when*: all three lanes create sealed issues on the fake (`properties[harbour.asAsked].words` is byte-exact in the proxy and provider tests). Both gaps have dispositions. The retirements landed. Budget and tripwire pass.

**Leftovers `Retires:` line:** checked. It names the `routes/proxy.js` `hashCredential` Waiting entry, and the diff removes both the entry (`docs/areas`) and the helper.

### Mutation checks (LIN-2274), each reverted, tree clean
| Mutation | Witness |
|---|---|
| Guard: comments walk always `[]` | red (1) |
| Guard: `description: undefined` | red (1); route repro 409→200 |
| proxy-writes: non-UUID → `continue` instead of 400 | red (2) |
| feedback: drop the `jira` env-default branch | red (1) |
| epic: always `parent` | red (2) |
| required-field 422 disabled | red (1) |
| property never sent | red (3) |
| session lane: `projectId` refusal disabled | red (1) |
| **issue type: drop the "Task" preference (`standard[0]`)** | **stays green** |

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is **"a present but malformed optional write field is silently dropped"** (`present: isUuid`). Create is fixed for all three fields. Its sibling is **PATCH** (`routes/proxy-writes.js:555–558`), which still drops a non-UUID `assigneeId`/`parentId`/`cycleId`. That is a ledger item below. A second class, "lanes spell 'undeclared field → 400' differently", is recorded as a Waiting entry in `docs/areas/web-routes.md`. It is outside this ticket: the shared create pipeline was explicitly excluded.

### Fixes for close-out
1. **`tests/unit/lin-4451-jira-create.test.js` ~line 117** ("creates a Task with its block sealed…"): the default `seed()` lists `TASK` first, so "Task is preferred" passes even with the preference removed. Make that test seed `seed({ types: [BUG, TASK, SUBTASK], fields: { [TASK.id]: SCREEN_TEAM_MANAGED, [BUG.id]: SCREEN_TEAM_MANAGED } })`, or add a separate test with that seed asserting `issuetype.id === TASK.id`. Confirm it goes red with `standard.find(t => t.name === 'Task') || standard[0]` reduced to `standard[0]`.
2. *(Recommended, same file)*: promote my route repro into a test under the Periodical-gate describe. Seed a gate-marked issue with `projectStatuses: { ENG: [{ id:'10100', name:'Task', subtask:false, statuses:[TODO, DONE] }] }` and `_transitions: [{ id:'31', name:'Done', to: DONE }]`, then `PATCH /api/proxy/issues/ENG-20 { stateId: 'done' }` through `buildProxyApp()`. Expect 409 `PERIODICAL_REPORT_NOT_PERSISTED`. Restore `jiraProvider.configure(savedJira)` in `afterEach`.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Live Jira accepts the create contract** (**inside**: the ticket's own claim). The claim covers `POST /rest/api/3/issue` with `properties`, the createmeta page keys (`issueTypes`/`fields`/`values`, `isLast`), the epic as `parent: { id }` on team-managed projects, Epic Link as the epic key on company-managed ones, and the re-read with `harbour.asAsked`. CI only exercises the fake. **After the deploy:** LIN-4452's live check on John's site. File a sealed task through proxy create, then GET the issue: the `harbour.asAsked` property holds the exact words and the description shows the formatted block. File one with `projectId` = an epic and confirm it reads back under that epic. A wrong result is a Jira 400 (surfaced as 422 "Jira refused the new issue"), a missing property, or an issue outside the epic.
- **Periodical gate against live Jira statuses** (**inside**: note 4). On the fake this is proven by my route repro, and by fix 2 once added. Live, it depends on `getProjectStatuses` mapping John's Done to `statusCategory: done`. **After the deploy:** LIN-4452's Periodical mint. Moving the minted task to Done with no report comment must give 409 `PERIODICAL_REPORT_NOT_PERSISTED`.
- **PATCH still silently drops a non-UUID `assigneeId`/`parentId`/`cycleId`** (**inside**: same idiom as the note-5 class this ticket bounded). **Before the merge**, choose one route. Either an explicit drop, with the reason that PATCH's documented convention is drop-on-200 (`routes/proxy-writes.js` ~559, LIN-2239; `lib/proxy-instructions.js:800`) and LIN-3807 (Backlog, "Proxy create and PATCH: refuse unknown or malformed fields with 400") already owns that contract change, recorded in the close-out summary with LIN-3807 linked as related. Or apply the create rule at `routes/proxy-writes.js:555–558` and update line 800. I recommend the explicit drop: it changes a documented contract that another ticket owns. The 16:23 comment's "follow-up" should name LIN-3807.
- **Jira feedback destination and screenshots** (**outside**: open product decisions, not creation correctness). With no body `teamId`, feedback files to the first Jira project, and a screenshot is a 422. Both are already recorded as Waiting entries in `docs/areas/providers.md` / `docs/areas/web-routes.md` (their home). Nothing more is needed here, and this is not a ticket: nothing is broken today.
- **Linear create behaviour change** (**inside**: disposition (b)). An external caller that sent `parentId: "LIN-123"` used to get a 201 without the parent and now gets a 400. No in-repo prompt or caller sends a non-UUID (checked `lib/prompts`, `lib/prompt-templates.js`, `lib/periodicals.js`), and `lib/proxy-instructions.js` plus `docs/proxy-integration.md` document the new rule. **A named monitor:** proxy event logs, 400 `"parentId must be a UUID"` / `"assigneeId must be a UUID"` / `"cycleId must be a UUID"` on `POST /api/proxy/issues`. Only production traffic shows whether outside agents relied on the drop. **Rollback:** revert the `uuid: true` lines in `routes/proxy-writes.js` (the commit that adds them), back to `present: isUuid`.
- **The Jira in-app form from an epic's "+ Add task" drops the epic** (**outside**: by plan design, since `createFields()` excludes `projectId`, the form does not render a project field and `/task/new?projectId=` is ignored). The task files in the chosen project with no epic. Home: a `## Waiting` entry in `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md`, worded: "`lib/render-task-create.js`: on Jira, '+ Add task' under an epic opens `/task/new?projectId=<epic>`, but `createFields()` has no `projectId`, so the epic is dropped silently; declare `projectId` in Jira's `createFields()` (the provider already sets the epic) or stop passing it. (LIN-4451 review.)"

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

Close-out should: make fix 1 (and preferably fix 2); record the PATCH drop with LIN-3807 linked, or make the PATCH change; write the `front-end-pages.md` Waiting entry; then re-check CI on the final commit before merging. The live items run after the deploy under LIN-4452.

## Blind read
Verdict: same. Better: token hashing now has one owner (`hashHarbourToken` in `lib/harbour-token-format.js`, used by the three stores and `routes/proxy.js`, with a test guarding it), and `routes/proxy-writes.js` now refuses a non-UUID `assigneeId`/`parentId`/`cycleId` instead of dropping it and still returning 201. Worse: `lib/providers/jira/index.js` now imports the Periodical gate from `lib/periodicals.js`, `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js` gained a `provider.name === 'jira'` branch, and the `ui.write` deep-link branch in `lib/render.js` is now dead code that a test still pins.

Read: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2429 at `466e8a462` against `2aab32bf0`.

### Inside the area, fix-sized
- `lib/providers/jira/fake-client.js` (providers): the new `listCreateIssueTypes`/`listCreateIssueTypeFields`/`createIssue` were inserted between `listLabels` and its JSDoc. "One page of the site-wide label vocabulary…" now sits above `listCreateIssueTypes`, and `listLabels` has no doc. Fix: move that comment back above `listLabels`.
- `lib/providers/jira/index.js` (providers): in `createIssue`, the comment on `BUILT_IN` says `parent` is one "the create never sets". But `_epicCreateField` does set `fields.parent` when the screen offers it. Fix: say instead that `parent` is excluded because only an epic supplies it, and that case is covered by `fieldId in fields`.
- `lib/periodicals.js` (llm-and-prompts): the scaffold header comment (line ~205) still calls the connector `"Write a Linear task…"`, but this change renamed it to "Write a task…". Fix: update the comment.
- `docs/proxy-integration.md` (agent-api, the doc for `routes/proxy-writes.js`): the new "**UUID-only fields**" paragraph was inserted inside the provider-compatibility list, before its last item. That leaves "- **Linear-backed workspaces** support every field above." stranded after the paragraph. Fix: move the paragraph below the Linear bullet.

### Inside the area, larger
- `lib/render.js` (front-end-pages): Linear, Local, GitHub and Jira all report `inlineCreate` now, and github-projects has `write: false`, so the `else if (isRealProject && ui.write)` deep-link branch can never run. `tests/unit/render.test.js` still pins that branch byte for byte, and `JiraProvider.getCreateTaskUrl` is kept only because `ui.write` is derived from whether the provider overrides it. That makes it a flag that looks like a feature. Larger: removing the branch means deciding what `ui.write` means now (`lib/providers/interface.js`) and whether every provider's `getCreateTaskUrl` override stays. That is a decision that touches several providers.
- `lib/providers/jira/index.js` (providers): `_fetchIssueGuard` now imports `extractPeriodicalGateId` from `lib/periodicals.js` to decide whether to fetch comments. So a provider depends on a prompts module, and the "is this issue gated" check now runs twice: here, and again in `refusedByPeriodicalGate` (`routes/proxy-writes.js`). Linear's guard just returns its last 20 comments every time. Larger: who owns that decision, whether the guard is told it is needed or the cost is accepted, is a design choice about the guard contract.
- `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js` (web-routes): `feedbackEnvDefault` hard-codes `provider?.name === 'jira'` to drop `FEEDBACK_TEAM_ID`/`FEEDBACK_PROJECT_ID`. The underlying fact is "this provider's ids are not Linear UUIDs". It belongs to the provider, and the next provider with that property will not learn it from a name check. Larger: it needs a decision about which provider capability or shape answers that question.
- `lib/providers/jira/index.js` (providers): `createFields()` leaves out `projectId` while `apiWriteFields()` includes it. So the in-app "+ Add task" link under an epic header (`/task/new?projectId=<epic id>`, from `lib/render.js`) has its epic silently dropped by `routes/task-create.js`, and the issue is filed outside the epic it was started from. Larger: whether the in-app form should offer an epic on Jira (project list scoped by team, form changes) is a product and design decision, not a line edit.

### Outside the area
None.

## Close-out — LIN-4451

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2429, merge commit `904719353b71595152b24260b357c1629c80b1e1`, pinned to head `5e29fb52b53df4026fe18bbb6002663c7db525f4`. Deployed: harbour.cat's page footer shows `904719353`, and the deployed `/api/proxy/instructions` carries the Jira create line and the UUID-only rule.

**How it meets what was asked:** per review's account (comment 575416b0), all three filing lanes (proxy, session, feedback) create sealed Jira issues on the fake, both review-note gaps (`parentId` = disposition (b), Periodical gate = fixed) are dispositioned, retirements landed, and the prompt budget and Periodical tripwire pass. The plan departures (no createmeta cache, screen-driven epic routing, kept `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` branch, no feedback env defaults on Jira) were accepted in review and are on LIN-4445.

description:
## As asked

Piece 2 of 3 of LIN-4445 (parent: "The loop works on Jira: Harbour can create Jira issues, and Jira can hold a task's sealed words"). This piece adds Jira issue creation, which opens all three filing lanes (proxy, session and feedback; Periodical mints and last-step filings use proxy create), and retires what creation makes obsolete. Blocked by piece 1 (the Jira seal). Read the parent's scope, Design and full Implementation Plan in LIN-4445's description ("## Implementation Plan" → "Session 2: creation", items 7–11), plus the "Plan Review Verdict" comment on LIN-4445 (notes 4 and 5 are dispositioned here).

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point. Follow it. Where the code shows it wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4445.

**Plan-review due:** no. Covered by LIN-4445's approving plan-review (comment 61e84035-1df2-459f-8def-5afdc7001e64, rev 1).
**Session fit:** fits one session.
**Grounding commit:** `4b5001ddf` (plan and review; no commits on the plan's paths since, re-checked at breakdown on 2026-11-13). Rebase onto piece 1 before starting.

### Approach

1. **Client:** `createIssue` (`POST /rest/api/3/issue` with `fields` + `properties`) and `getCreateMeta` (`GET /rest/api/3/issue/createmeta/{projectKey}/issuetypes`, then that type's fields). `fake-client.js` gains create and createmeta.
2. **Provider** `createIssue` in `lib/providers/jira/index.js` creates, then re-reads (with `properties=harbour.asAsked`) and returns the canonical issue, as `updateIssue` does. The property comes from `splitAsAsked` of the given description, because every lane has already sealed it. It uses piece 1's shared size function.
   * `createFields()` becomes `title`, `description`, `teamId`. `teamId` resolves as a Jira project key (LIN-2018) through `resolveTeamInput`.
   * `apiWriteFields()` adds `projectId`, an epic: `parent` on team-managed projects, or the Epic Link field through `_resolveEpicLinkFieldId` on company-managed ones. **Do not declare** `stateId`: a transition after create is a second, non-atomic write.
   * `parentId` **(review note 5):** proxy create forwards `parentId` only when it is a UUID (`routes/proxy-writes.js` \~451–459, `present: isUuid`), and the session lane never forwards it. As things stand, a Jira parent would be silently dropped. Pick one disposition, state the reason, and don't advertise subtask support until it's resolved: (a) accept the provider's own id form when the provider declares `parentId`; (b) refuse a non-UUID `parentId` with 400 instead of dropping it; or (c) leave `parentId` out of `apiWriteFields()` and file a follow-up ticket. Provider subtask-type tests alone are not evidence of end-to-end subtask filing.
3. **Issue type, chosen inside the provider with no new setting:** prefer "Task", else the first standard non-subtask type at hierarchy level 0, and a subtask type when there's a parent. A required field without a default, beyond summary, project, issuetype, description, reporter and parent, returns **422 naming the field(s)** before anything is created. Cache briefly per site and project, with the site in the key.
4. **Periodical report gate (review note 4):** Jira's `issueWriteGuard` (\~1016) returns neither `description` nor recent comments, so `refusedByPeriodicalGate` (`routes/proxy-writes.js` \~547) never fires on Jira. Recommended: add `description` (through piece 1's composed reader) and the last 20 comments to Jira's `issueWriteGuard` from the same `getIssue`, matching Linear (`linear/index.js` \~1745, LIN-694). If you judge it out of scope, file a ticket instead and say why.
5. **UI:** `ui.inlineCreate` turns true by itself through `supports('createIssue')`, so `lib/render.js` shows the in-app form. **Keep the** `getCreateTaskUrl` **override**: `ui.write` derives from it (`lib/providers/interface.js`), and removing it hides "+ Add task".
6. **Retires** (every change names what it retires):
   * the deep-link create path on Jira, and `inlineCreate: false`
   * the stale LIN-1557 "no native Jira team" comments in `index.js` (header \~13–46, capability profile, `getCreateTaskUrl`, `ui` \~1328–1356)
   * README's "creating new issues isn't supported yet" (\~line 60) and its sealing line (\~89)
   * `docs/proxy-integration.md`'s "Jira files unsealed" (\~2070), and its `parentId` UUID-only line (\~2065) if disposition (a) or (b) changes that
   * `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s "where the provider cannot create tickets" branch in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`
   * the "Linear task" wording in `lib/periodicals.js` (\~251, \~278), which becomes provider-neutral
   * repeatable check: `grep -rn "LIN-1557\|cannot create tickets\|Jira.*unsealed\|isn't supported yet" lib routes docs README.md`. Each remaining hit is either retired or cited as still true.
7. **Prompt re-measure:** rebase first, then re-measure against `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` and the Periodical hash in `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js`. Cite LIN-4445 beside any ceiling raised (area lesson LIN-4393).

### Testing strategy (witnesses)

* Provider tests against the fake: create; create with an epic (team-managed and company-managed); create with a block (property present, re-read `kept`, byte-exact words); create with a parent, only if disposition (a) is taken.
* Issue type: Task preferred; no Task; subtask; a required custom field refused with its name and nothing created; cache key includes the site.
* End to end on the Jira fake: session (`task-create-route`), proxy create (including a Periodical-mint shape with a project key as team) and the feedback lane.
* The Periodical gate fires on Jira (if note 4 is taken in scope).
* Updated pins: `providers.test.js`, `jira-provider.test.js`, `render.test.js`, `render-task-create.test.js`, `task-create-route.test.js`.

### Done when

All three lanes create sealed Jira issues on the fake. The `parentId` and Periodical-gate gaps each have an explicit disposition (a fix or a filed ticket). The retirements land, and the prompt budget and Periodical tripwire pass after rebase.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Jira gains issue creation, which opens the proxy, session and feedback lanes with sealed words, plus explicit parent and Periodical-gate dispositions and the retirements creation makes stale; the Surveys' findings land inside those lanes or stay nearby.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implemented (close-out stub)

Merged in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2429](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2429>) (merge commit 904719353b71595152b24260b357c1629c80b1e1) and deployed. Jira `createIssue` opens the proxy, session and feedback filing lanes with sealed words; the Periodical report gate fires on Jira; the retirements landed. Implemented as planned on LIN-4445 with the departures recorded there (no createmeta cache, screen-driven epic routing, kept `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` branch, no feedback env defaults on Jira, `parentId` disposition (b)). The live check on John's Jira is LIN-4452. The full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the plan, review and close-out history is in the comment trail.
